title: Gate graded against full ground truth: recall 1.00 (both wins, incl. uncalibrated locale-sum), precision 0.50 — FPs are the pretraining blind spot
summary: First full grading of the context-need gate (lib/context-gate.js, default thresholds) against all 9 ground-truth cases from the held-out arc, run offline over the live KB (154 embedded notes). Confusion: TP=2 FN=0 FP=2 TN=5 → recall 1.00, precision 0.50. KEY POSITIVE: locale-sum (win #2) fires correctly and was NEVER used in calibration (gate was tuned only on task→transcript) — a passed generalization test. Zero missed wins. THE TWO FPs (wt-gc cos 0.738, tls-local gap 0.413) are structural, not tuning misses: genuinely relevant empirical notes exist for those tasks, but the model already knows the facts from pretraining (Phase 1's third boundary condition). The gate measures note↔task AFFINITY — necessary but not sufficient; it cannot see the model's prior. ERROR-COST ASYMMETRY makes this the right operating point: false-inject costs the bounded over-deliberation tax (few k output tokens, solve rate unaffected); false-abstain costs a failed task (0/8 edges). Recall-perfect/precision-loose is the correct side of the trade. KNOWN FIX (next, contained, offline): add a PROJECT-LOCALITY score on the note (measured numbers like '~40%', error strings, local file/identifier names) alongside affinity — the two winning notes are dense with project-local specifics, the two FP notes are general-infra phrased; likely separable. Use this 9-case set as the regression suite. Eval script pattern: gateTask(task={label,spec}, overlayNotesWithVecs, {embedQuery:embed, cosine}).
